### Problem: Number of Different Subsequences GCDs {#sec-gcd-p3-subseq}

::: {.p-statement}
**Which gcds are reachable?** Given an integer array `nums`, find the number of **distinct
greatest-common-divisor values** over all non-empty **subsequences** (not necessarily
contiguous) of `nums`.

```text
nums = [6, 10, 3]  -> 5
```

The subsequence gcds you can realize are $6, 10, 3$ (single elements), $\gcd(6,10)=2$, and
$\gcd(3,6)=3, \gcd(6,10,3)=1$ - the distinct values are $\{1, 2, 3, 6, 10\}$, i.e. $5$.

**Constraints.** $1 \le n \le 10^5$; $1 \le \mathit{nums}[i] \le 10^5$.
Source: [LC 1819 · Number of Different Subsequences GCDs](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-different-subsequences-gcds/){.solved difficulty="Hard"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Enumerating $2^n$ subsequences is hopeless, but the *set of gcd values* is tiny: folding a
gcd over a growing set can only produce divisors of numbers already in the array. That
gives two views. The **forward** view folds a set - keep the set of gcds of subsequences
seen so far, and when a new element $x$ arrives the only new gcds are $x$ itself and
$\gcd(g, x)$ for each existing $g$; the set stays small because gcds collapse fast. The
**backward** view asks a different question: for a target $d$, is $d$ achievable? Exactly
when the gcd of *all array elements that are multiples of $d$* equals $d$ - because their
subsequence gcd is the finest thing a multiple-of-$d$ subsequence can reach. Sieving the
value domain by divisibility (@sec-gcd-a4) turns that into a $\sum_d V/d$ harmonic loop.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Fold a set of gcds forward.** For each element, adjoin it and its gcds with every gcd
   already collected; the final set size is the answer. $O(n \cdot S \log V)$ with a small
   reachable set $S$.
2. **Sieve the value domain backward.** For every $d$ from $1$ to $\max$, fold the gcd of all
   present multiples of $d$; $d$ is achievable iff that fold equals $d$. $O(V \log V)$.
:::

::: {#fig-gcd-p3-subseq}

```{python}

#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    V.grid(ax, p, [["divisor d", "1", "2", "3", "6", "10"],
                   ["gcd of multiples", "1", "2", "3", "6", "10"],
                   ["achievable?", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes"]],
           colors={(2, 1): "green", (2, 2): "green", (2, 3): "green",
                   (2, 4): "green", (2, 5): "green"}, cell_w=1.15)
V.show(draw)
```

For `nums = [6, 10, 3]` the only present multiples of $2$ are $6, 10$ whose gcd is $2$ - so
$2$ is reachable. Every divisor whose "gcd of its multiples" equals itself is counted; there
are $5$ of them.

:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Fold a set of gcds forward

::: {.form-next}
Maintain `all` - the distinct gcds of all subsequences of the prefix. Adjoining $x$ adds
subsequences $\{x\}$ and (each old subsequence) $\cup \{x\}$, whose gcds are $x$ and
$\gcd(g,x)$ for each $g$ in `all`. The set never blows up because gcds collide.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("subseq", "fold")
    assert str(final) == "5"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def sq_fold(nums):
    allset = set()
    for x in nums:
        new = {x} | {math.gcd(g, x) for g in allset}
        allset |= new
    return len(allset)

assert sq_fold([6, 10, 3]) == 5
```

##### C++

```cpp
long long mygcd(long long a, long long b) {
    while (b) { long long t = a % b; a = b; b = t; }
    return a;
}

int sqFold(vector<int>& nums) {
    vector<int> all;
    for (int x : nums) {
        int sz = (int) all.size();
        all.push_back(x);
        for (int i = 0; i < sz; ++i) all.push_back((int) mygcd(all[i], x));
        sort(all.begin(), all.end());
        all.erase(unique(all.begin(), all.end()), all.end());
    }
    return (int) all.size();
}
```

:::

#### Sieve the value domain backward

::: {.form-next}
Flip the question. $d$ is a reachable gcd iff the gcd of all present multiples of $d$ is
exactly $d$. Walk $d = 1 \ldots \max$ and gather multiples in a harmonic loop
$\sum_{d} \max/d$; fold their gcd and compare to $d$. This is the $\binom{\cdot}{\cdot}$
sieve behind @sec-gcd-a4 and it is $O(V \log V)$ independent of $n$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("subseq", "sieve")
    assert str(final) == "5"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def sq_sieve(nums):
    present = set(nums); mx = max(nums); cnt = 0
    for d in range(1, mx + 1):
        mult = [x for x in range(d, mx + 1, d) if x in present]
        if not mult:
            continue
        col = 0
        for x in mult:
            col = math.gcd(col, x)
        if col == d:
            cnt += 1
    return cnt

assert sq_sieve([6, 10, 3]) == 5
for _ in range(200):
    a = [random.randint(1, 30) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 8))]
    assert sq_sieve(a) == sq_fold(a)
```

##### C++

```cpp
long long mygcd(long long a, long long b) {
    while (b) { long long t = a % b; a = b; b = t; }
    return a;
}

int sqSieve(vector<int>& nums) {
    int mx = *max_element(nums.begin(), nums.end());
    vector<int> present(mx + 1, 0);
    for (int x : nums) present[x] = 1;
    int cnt = 0;
    for (int d = 1; d <= mx; ++d) {
        int col = 0; bool any = false;
        for (int m = d; m <= mx; m += d)
            if (present[m]) { col = (int) mygcd(col, m); any = true; }
        if (any && col == d) ++cnt;
    }
    return cnt;
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Time.** Rung 1 is $O(n \cdot S \log V)$ with the reachable-set size $S$; rung 2 is
$O(V \log V)$ where $V = \max(\mathit{nums}) \le 10^5$. **Space.** $O(V)$ for the presence
array (rung 2) or $O(S)$ for the set (rung 1).
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- **All identical.** `nums = [7, 7, 7]`: every subsequence has gcd $7$, so exactly one
  distinct value is reachable and the answer is $1$. The sieve marks only $d = 7$ (its
  present multiples fold to $7$) and skips $d = 1$ (present multiples $\{7\}$ fold to
  $7 \ne 1$).
- **A 1 in the array.** Any subsequence that contains a lone $1$ alongside others folds to
  $1$, so $1$ becomes a reachable value and the set grows by exactly that one element.
- **Duplicates.** The presence *set* ignores repeats; folding over distinct multiples is
  enough because gcd is idempotent.

**Debug tip.** If the two rungs disagree, your sieve counted $d$ when it should test the gcd
of multiples *equal to* $d$ - a divisor common to all multiples but larger than $d$ means $d$
is not itself a minimal reachable value.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Treating the subsequence as a *subarray*. Contiguity is irrelevant here; only the multiset
  of chosen values matters.
- Counting the empty subsequence. The fold seed `{x}` correctly starts from single
elements; never prime `allset` with a $0$ that would add a spurious $\gcd(0, g) = g$.
:::

**Variants.** @sec-gcd-p3-gcdpair also sieves the value domain by divisor but *counts pairs*
per bucket; @sec-gcd-p2-split folds gcd over contiguous segments instead of subsequences.
